narrative.northStar: The Park Table at Golden Hour
narrative.overview: A real stone chess table in a park, drawn live in 3D: low sun through a canopy over a polished granite slab with an inlaid travertine and slate board and carved alabaster and basalt pieces. The UI is the shade around it; sunlight is the only accent, and every move lands with the weight of stone.
keyCharacteristics: The 3D table is the only lit object; the UI is flat shade with hairlines.
Sunlight means active, in the UI and in the scene.
Impact escalates: move, capture (hit-stop, knock-off), check (shudder), mate (slow-motion topple).
A transparent DOM board over the 3D board keeps input, focus and accessibility; WebGL-less browsers get the same grid as a 2D board.
Hahmlet for stone-cut type (titles, results, clocks), Pretendard for the rest.

rules.name: The Light Means Active Rule
rules.body: Sunlight marks only what is active now: the running clock, the primary action, the selection, the targets, the latest move.

rules.name: The Shade Rule
rules.body: UI surfaces are flat shade with hairlines; no colored glows, glass or decorative gradients.

rules.name: The Keep-All Rule
rules.body: Korean text uses word-break: keep-all so words never split across lines.

rules.name: The Escalation Rule
rules.body: Effects scale with the event; a quiet move never shakes like a capture.

dos: Do keep sunlight for the active thing.
Do act out every board change; snap when it is not one move.
Do keep every control in the DOM.
Do scale impact with the event.
donts: Don't put colored glows, glass or gradients on UI surfaces.
Don't imitate materials in CSS; material lives in the scene.
Don't use cards, pills or radii above 6px.
Don't let the scene cover the status, the clocks or a primary action.
Don't use a browser confirm() or alert(); use the confirm bar.
